sections.title: The Priestly Garments
observations: Exodus 28 begins with God's instructions for the garments of the priests, specifically Aaron and his sons. These garments are not merely functional but are designed to reflect the holiness and glory of God.
The high priest's attire includes the ephod, breastpiece, robe, tunic, turban, and sash, each with specific materials and designs. This emphasizes the importance of beauty and dignity in worship.
The ephod, made of gold, blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, symbolizes the priest's role as a mediator between God and the people.

sections.title: The Breastpiece of Judgment
observations: The breastpiece, also known as the breastplate of judgment, contains twelve stones representing the twelve tribes of Israel. This signifies that the high priest carries the names of the tribes before God, highlighting his intercessory role.
The Urim and Thummim, placed in the breastpiece, are tools for divining God's will, showing the priest's responsibility to seek divine guidance for the nation.

sections.title: The Robe and Other Garments
observations: The robe of the ephod is to be made entirely of blue, symbolizing the heavens and God's presence. The pomegranates and bells on the hem serve as reminders of the priest's duties and the need for holiness in approaching God.
The tunic, sash, and turban are also described, emphasizing the need for the priests to be set apart and to reflect God's holiness in their appearance.

sections.title: Consecration of the Priests
observations: The chapter concludes with instructions for the consecration of Aaron and his sons. This process involves anointing them and setting them apart for their sacred duties, underscoring the seriousness of their role in the worship of God.
The rituals of consecration highlight the need for purity and dedication in serving God, which is a principle that extends to all believers today.

importantVerses.commentary: The garments are for glory and beauty, reflecting God's holiness and the dignity of the priestly office.
Aaron shall bear the names of the sons of Israel on his heart, symbolizing his intercessory role before God.

questions: What do the specific materials and designs of the priestly garments teach us about the nature of worship?
How does the role of the high priest in the Old Testament foreshadow the work of Christ as our High Priest?
In what ways can we apply the principles of consecration and holiness in our own lives today?
